Paraesthesias have been re- ported with pentamidine therapy. Perioral numbness occurred in a patient soon after starting the third intravenous infusion of pen- tamidine for treatment of pneumocystis pneumonia and disap- peared after the end of the infusion; numbness recurred with all subsequent pentamidine infusions.1 1. Milligan KS, Phillips DL. Perioral numbness associated with in- travenous pentamidine administration. Ann Pharmacother 2007; 41: 153–6. Effects on the respiratory system. Although inhaled penta- midine has produced reactions that are normally associated with the parenteral route, the main problem after inhalation is bron- choconstriction;1 it can be prevented by prior use of a bronchodi- lator. Acute eosinophilic pneumonia associated with nebulised pentamidine has been reported in a patient.2 Concern has also been expressed at the risks to those who are with the patient at the time of inhalation and are exposed to nebulised pentamidine.3-5 1.
